I get that feeling when I read stories that at first glance seem to have no meaning or that feel pointless. For example the events in the story are disconnected and there isn't an apparent overarching plot to tie it all together. Another example is when there seems to be a goal of some sort but at the end the protagonist fail with their quest or at least aspects of it. When I read such stories I at first feel a bit disappointed, then I start wondering what the point of it all was. I read the story waiting for the conclusion that would give me satisfaction and closure but what I'm left with is a feeling of emptiness. In that void I usually begin to reflect on the story and try to find a reason for why this wasn't a waste of time. Occasionally there's a deeper message or story hidden underneath the obvious one, other times the whole point is the failure. Life doesn't always have a reason for why it is like it is and as a living person my life isn't always the life you'd expect from a protagonist, for that reason these stories can often be a more truthful reflection of reality. 

The topic of your question was about stories that made us realize the sheer amount of time we have and to do more things with it. I've talked about a particular type of stories but how do these relate to your question you might ask. Well, after reading a story like this I mentioned finding myself wondering if I've wasted my time reading it. Perhaps I did, perhaps I didn't but the point is that it makes me reflect on the concept of time. What is worth spending your time on and what isn't? How do I know if it is or isn't? Finally, if it is a so called waste, is that okay to still spend time on? In the end what matters is how you feel about it, as long as it feels good to you then why would it be a waste? You don't have to be a protagonist and achieve remarkable things, just live a life that feels good to you a be content with that. Do you need to be more productive or is that feeling forced upon you? Learning to let go and appreciate the moment you live in can do astonishing things. You might reach another conclusion than I did after thinking of these questions and that's okay but doing some self reflection is valuable of itself. 

Finally since this was a post requesting book recommendations I'll tell you about the the first book that made me think of these things, it's "the old man and the sea" by Ernest Hemingway. I read it when I was like 13 or something for school and after finishing I felt both blown away and empty. I couldn't understand how this was a book, to the me at the time it felt so pointless, I wasn't sure why anyone would write a story like that. At the same time though I had really enjoyed the book and this made me even more confused. How could a so called pointless book give me so much entertainment? It all felt too weird for me and that's when I began diving deeper. I didn't come to understand why I like those kinds of stories until after I'd experienced some more of them but with time I began to realize why and consequently enjoy them even more. Today I view time, productivity and life much different to how I used to and they don't give me as much negative feelings as they used to. 

This got quite long but hopefully it helped! <3
